case_name: State of Himachal Pradesh and another v Raj Kumar Chopra
petitioner: State of Himachal Pradesh and another
respondent:
Raj Kumar Chopra
Supreme Court of India

19 April 1994
Cr.A. Nos. 615 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 10 January 1984 of the Himachal Pradesh High Court in Cr. A. No. 21 of 1983) and 616 (From the Judgment and Order Dt. 10 January 1984 of the Himachal Pradesh High Court in Cr. A. No. 21 of 1983) of 1984
The Judgment was delivered by : K. Jayachandra Reddy, J.
1.  These two appeals, one by the State and the other by Shri M.L. Chadha, father of the deceased, are filed against the judgment of the High Court acquitting the respondents-accused. The trial court convicted them under Sections 302/34 IPC and sentenced each of them to undergo imprisonment for life. The appeal preferred by them was allowed by the High Court and they were acquitted.
2.  The prosecution case is as follows. Shri R.K. Chopra, A-2 is the father and Mrs Santosh Chopra, A-3 is the mother of A-1 Anil Chopra. The deceased Mrs Kiran Chopra was married to A-1 in the year 1981 who was
facts: The trial court convicted them under Sections 302/34 IPC and sentenced each of them to undergo imprisonment for life.
A-2 retired from service in July 1981, and he and his wife A-3 also joined A-1 and the deceased at Rajban and continued to live there.
On 20-8-1982, A-1 used to come home for lunch on working days, and after lunch he returned to his office at 2 p.m.
The deceased received her medical treatment throughout at Harbertpur Mission Hospital but her condition started deteriorating.
PW 12 lodged a report with police alleging that the deceased told him that the three accused persons poured kerosene on her and set fire for not bringing adequate dowry.
issues: Whether the dying declaration recorded by PW 5 is a fabricated one?
Whether there is sufficient evidence to establish the motive of the accused
Whether the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt
petitioner_arguments: There are no grounds whatsoever to doubt the veracity of PW 5.
The plea of the defence that the death was due to an accident, cannot be ruled out.
These are appeals against acquittal and the High Court has given good reasons for acquitting the respondents.
court_reasoning: The High Court has discussed his evidence in great detail and in our view has rightly held that there are no grounds whatsoever to doubt the veracity of PW 5.

The police officers incharge of Police Post, Rajban and Police Station, Paonta Sahib evinced undue interest and went out of their way in fabricating the evidence to involve the accused in a case under Section 302 IPC.
Therefore it cannot be concluded that the police evinced undue interest and went out of the way and fabricated the evidence.
holding: The prosecution has not proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
The High Court has given good reasons for acquitting the respondents.
Accordingly both these appeals are dismissed.
